analyzed_vuln.description: Double-free is caused by ownership confusion for alias flag arrays. parse_aliasf() decodes each AF entry via decode_flags() and stores the allocated pointer in aliasf[]. Later, dictionary entries may reference these alias pointers as pt->astr. free_table() calls free_flag(pt->astr, pt->alen), and free_flag() skips delete only when aliasf is non-empty and ONLYUPCASEFLAG is not set. For entries whose alias flag vector includes ONLYUPCASEFLAG, free_flag() incorrectly deletes pt->astr even though it points into aliasf storage. Then HashMgr::~HashMgr() unconditionally deletes aliasf[] again, producing double free. Crash is observed in destructor, but root cause is the invalid ownership/free policy interaction introduced through aliasf pointers created in parse_aliasf() and consumed by free_flag().
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires an affix file that defines AF aliases (so aliasf is populated) and dictionary/entries that use an alias index whose decoded flag vector contains ONLYUPCASEFLAG (in FLAG long mode this can be crafted from two-byte flag values). Data flow: affdicfuzzer input -> load_config() parses AF via parse_aliasf()/decode_flags() -> alias pointer reused as hentry::astr via get_aliasf() path -> object teardown calls free_table()->free_flag() (first free) and then ~HashMgr aliasf cleanup (second free).
